subject: SIG packaging: OneTrust bulk manifest + chunked PDF upload plan
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T10:12:00Z
Subject: SIG packaging - evidence upload constraints

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the initial SIG responses. Procurement has a few practical requirements for evidence we need to confirm before the portal upload:

- OneTrust wants each PDF as an individual file (no multi-doc combined PDFs) OR a single package with a manifest CSV describing page offsets.
- Max upload size per file is 250MB; they accept chunked uploads but require a stable manifest (checksum per chunk).
- The portal requires the evidence_index field to match our CSV headers exactly (document_id, page_start, page_end, control_ids).

Can Redwood provide a manifest + per-document checksums and tell us whether you plan to: (A) split multi-section docs into per-control PDFs, or (B) keep consolidated PDFs and provide a page-index manifest?

Also confirm ETA for upload to OneTrust (Procurement wants this in the next 7 business days).

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Park
Senior Sourcing Manager, AcmeCloud
emily.park@acmecloud.com

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
To: Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sergio.alvarez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-02T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG packaging - evidence upload constraints

Emily —

Appreciate the detail. Short answers up front: we will provide a OneTrust-compatible manifest CSV, per-file SHA256 checksums, and we plan option (B): keep consolidated PDFs and deliver a page-index manifest that maps control IDs to page ranges. That minimizes risk of missed context in proofs (audit logs and process docs are multi-page).

Plan outline (high level):
1) Generate consolidated PDFs from our SIG repository (flattened, with bookmarks).
2) Produce a manifest CSV (onetrust_bulk_manifest.csv) with columns: document_id, filename, sha256_hex, page_count, page_start, page_end, control_refs.
3) Split large files into 200MB chunked parts only when necessary and include chunk_index, chunk_sha256 in the manifest. We'll use resumable chunked upload endpoints for OneTrust.
4) Deliver evidence_index_map.xlsx to show per-control page ranges for procurement review.

Attachments: I attached a working draft manifest and an example PDF (SIG_answers_v3.pdf) with bookmarks and a small zip of chunked test files. Please review the CSV header expectations and confirm if Procurement will accept a manifest that references chunked parts rather than separate single-file uploads.

ETA: we can complete the first-package export + manifest by COB Tuesday (2027-11-05) if that works for your upload window.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Sr. Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
diego.fernandez@redwood.com

[Attachment: SIG_answers_v3.pdf (PDF, 1.9MB)]

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com, Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG packaging - evidence upload constraints

Diego / Emily —

I reviewed the draft manifest and did a small proof upload to a sandbox OneTrust instance. Notes and suggested changes attached:

- Manifest header must include: upload_job_id, submitter, platform_version — adding these prevents portal validation rejections.
- Use SHA256 for both file and chunk artifacts and include a file-level "combined_sha256" column for the assembled PDF to make post-upload verification straightforward.
- Add a note column with redwood_internal_doc_id so procurement can reference our internal evidence tracker.
- For any PDF over 180 pages, OneTrust sometimes times out on preview; we should add a thumbnails.zip in the package (small images of first page per document).

I've attached evidence_index_map.xlsx with sample control->page mappings for SIG_A. If procurement accepts the chunk manifest approach, we should:
- Export consolidated PDFs from the repo, flatten annotations, generate per-page OCR layer for searchability.
- If a file needs chunking, create chunk_n files named filename.partNN and list them in manifest with chunk_index and chunk_sha256.

Attaching my checklist: evidence_index_map.xlsx and the revised manifest CSV (onetrust_bulk_manifest.csv).

Marissa Cole
Compliance Delivery Lead
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: evidence_index_map.xlsx (XLSX, 42KB)]
[Attachment: onetrust_bulk_manifest.csv (CSV, 9KB) — revised]

From: Emily Park <emily.park@acmecloud.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, Procurement Ops <procurement@acmecloud.com>
Date: 2027-11-03T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG packaging - evidence upload constraints

Thanks — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications from Procurement:

- The portal team insists the manifest rows map to the final uploaded file names visible in the UI. If you submit chunked parts, they need the assembled_filename column so we can map previews back to the consolidated doc.
- Will Redwood provide the thumbnails.zip? Procurement is willing to accept a single thumbnails.zip as part of the package.
- For the CSV encoding: UTF-8 with CRLF line endings.

Procurement's tentative window: they will create the OneTrust job next Friday (2027-11-12). If Redwood can upload the package before that date we can avoid manual review blocks.

Emily
